selection: Up to 12 worlds per measured category; same source audit and request join as steering-examples.json; descending stability, then question length and record ID.

examples.question: Which labeled tile contains a completely filled 2-by-2 cyan square? Answer A, B, C, or D.
Which half of the centered dashboard visibly contains the steering wheel? Answer left or right.
Is the central hole's diameter greater than the colored rim's thickness on one side? Answer yes or no.
Which labeled tile looks exactly the same after a quarter-turn (90 degree) rotation? Answer A, B, C, or D.
Which colored patch contains a square joined edge-to-edge to colored squares above, below, left, and right?
If the colored junction is removed, does the remaining visible network become disconnected? Answer yes or no.
What color is the snowman's single filled triangular nose? Answer orange, blue, or purple from the visible pixels.
If the colored wall tile is erased, does it create a new connection between the two white chambers? Answer yes or no.
Inside the navy stamp, can you trace one unbroken cream channel from the green dot to the orange dot? Answer connected or broken.
Does the single hash-style glyph visibly have exactly two near-horizontal crossbars crossing both upright stems? Answer yes or no.
A reversed patch in the fine checker texture reveals one hidden silhouette. Is its boundary round or four-sided? Answer round or four-sided.
Treat black and yellow as one land shape. If the yellow patch is removed, will the remaining black land split into two pieces? Answer yes or no.
Does the one dark track contain a closed route? Ignore the colored dots. Answer yes or no.
The dark trail is one connected thin stroke. How many separate pale pockets does its complete route enclose: one pocket or two pockets?
The black ink is one connected thin drawing that encloses exactly two white pockets. Is one white pocket nested inside the other? Answer yes or no.
How many separate white pockets are fully enclosed by the single dark paperclip stroke? Count only white regions completely surrounded by the stroke.
Starting at the ringed end, number every corner along the cyan trace from 1. Reconnect corners 1, 3, 5, 7, and 9 in order. Which symbol appears: M or W?
Following the single blue S-shaped stroke from its top endpoint to its bottom endpoint, which bend order is visible: right then left, or left then right?
Can the entire connected blue network be traced in one continuous stroke without lifting and without retracing any segment? Answer possible or impossible.
Starting at the arrowhead and following the colored USB trunk toward its round base, which side branch joins the trunk first—left or right? Answer left or right.
Follow the dark-blue route from the coral start dot to the blue finish dot. Across its five bends, are there more left turns or right turns? Answer left or right.
Relative to the imaginary straight line joining its two round endpoints, does more signed area of the cyan route lie above or below the line? Answer above or below.
Imagine the straight chord joining the colored mini-trace's two endpoints. Excluding the endpoints, how many times does the trace cross that chord? Answer 1, 2, or 3.
Following the teal mini-profile from left to right, which flat extreme occurs first: its highest plateau (PEAK) or its lowest plateau (TROUGH)? Answer PEAK or TROUGH.
Do the two visible irises have the same color? Answer yes or no.
Do the top coral interval and bottom blue interval share any horizontal values? Answer yes or no.
Do the coral and blue needles lean in the same horizontal direction as they rise? Answer yes or no.
Do all three separated colored curve fragments trace parts of one imaginary circle? Answer yes or no.
Which color pair of broken rings has its two gaps facing each other? Answer red, blue, green, or purple.
Align the two colored 7x7 tiles. Keep only positions dark in both. Which symbol remains: X, plus, T, or L?
Do the two circular tail lamps on the rear of the car visibly have the same solid fill color? Answer yes or no.
Which colored pair has its vertical midpoint closer to the gold reference dot: coral or blue? Answer coral or blue.
Trace the dark closed loop. Are the two cyan checkpoints consecutive around the loop, with no orange checkpoint between them?
How many separate dark circular finger holes are visible inside the colored bowling ball? Count only circles fully inside the ball.
In the highlighted calibration inset, does the diamond target lie strictly between the two vertical endpoint ticks? Answer yes or no.
Compare BEFORE with AFTER. Exactly one lettered lamp changed between hollow and filled. Which lettered lamp changed? Answer A, B, or C.
Which symbol is hidden by the texture: a circle or a diamond?
Apply the marked clockwise spiral and adjacent-pair XOR. Is the resulting bitmap A) LOOP or B) DIAMOND? Answer A or B.
How many horizontal stripes are visible on the flag? Count every full-width or canton-shortened horizontal stripe once.
Is the center of area of the single filled region above or below the dashed horizontal reference line? Answer above or below.
On which side of the striped flag is the solid blue rectangular canton: left or right? Answer left or right from the visible image.
Inside the outlined circular medallion, do the dark and light colored regions cover the same area? Ignore the outline. Answer yes or no.
For each red pin, compare the cyan areas on its two sides and keep the smaller area. Which panel has the largest such smaller-side area?
Inside the violet frame, blur the tiny checker texture until individual checks disappear. Which symbol remains: X, plus, diamond, or ring?
The colored plaque has one circular opening. Relative to the center of the plaque's outer circle, is the opening shifted left or right? Answer left or right.
Treat every visible cyan part of the plate as having equal weight. Which colored pin is nearest the plate's center of area? Answer red, gold, violet, or green.
Which way does the large colored play triangle point—left or right? Judge its broad face and single tip; ignore the gray player controls. Answer left or right.
Is the colored specimen's filled area spread more horizontally or vertically about the gold center marker? Count all colored area. Answer horizontal or vertical.
Which colored bead lies on the only closed loop of the cyan rail?
How many times does the cyan trace cross the dashed reference line? Answer with a number.
How many high arches are visible in this handwritten lowercase m? Count each distinct crest that rises above the dashed guide.
The blue line is one closed wavy loop. Count its large outward bulges around the whole loop. Does it have four lobes or five lobes?
In the boxed trace, as x increases, do the seven straight pieces alternate rising and falling at every interior bend? Answer yes or no.
Which labeled stretch of the continuous rail has four square bumps whose centers are equally spaced from left to right? Answer A, B, C, or D.
Following the arrow from the purple start marker to the gray terminal cap, which checkpoint comes first: orange or teal? Answer orange or teal.
Follow the single dark route from the orange start marker. Which colored destination marker does the route connect to? Answer red, blue, or green.
How many self-crossings are visible in the single colored practice trace? Count only places where four colored arms meet, and answer 1, 2, 3, or 4.
From top to bottom, do the visible top strands at the five crossings of the single blue shoelace follow this exact sequence: /, \, /, \, /? Answer yes or no.
Follow the cyan route from the coral start dot to the blue finish dot. Does the route reach its highest point before its lowest point? Answer before or after.
Follow the single blue trail from its tight inner end toward its wide outer end. Does it wind clockwise or counterclockwise? Answer clockwise or counterclockwise.
Which labeled card has four cyan dots at the corners of a rectangle? Answer A, B, C, or D.
How many complete colored rings are visible in the sports emblem? Count each colored closed loop once.
Which colored plaque has the smaller top clearance around its window: amber or teal? Answer amber or teal.
Which sample increases more from BEFORE to AFTER: coral or blue? Upward movement is an increase. Answer coral or blue.
Four separate broken rings form a quartet. Do all four open gaps face the common center of the quartet? Answer yes or no.
Trace the navy trail touching each green start. Do the two trails end at the same terminal color? Answer same or different.
Each card contains one cyan island and one amber island. Which card has equal visible area in its two islands? Answer A, B, C, or D.
Across the two separated mini-plots, is the combined number of trace crossings of the dashed baselines odd or even? Answer odd or even.
Oppose each candidate tile's opening direction and reverse its three-tile order. Which candidate reproduces all three directions in R: A or B?
Reading the black keys from left to right, are they arranged as a separated group of two followed by a separated group of three? Answer yes or no.
Trace each navy network from its green ring to its red ring, ignoring dead-end branches. Which green-to-red route is longer along the network: top or bottom?
Reading clockwise from the top, do the four large black clock-face numerals appear in the order 12, 3, 6, 9? Ignore the small gray tick marks. Answer yes or no.
Do all four arms of the single colored plus sign extend equally far from its center? Answer yes or no.
Which candidate has the same five-station height profile as the reference when read from right to left?
Which ringed checkpoint—amber or violet—is closer to the halfway point of the thick green-to-red ribbon?
How many straight sides does the red STOP sign face have? Count only the outer edges of the red sign face.
Which half of the single connected filled basin contains more inked area: left or right? Answer left or right.
Which sector contains the only lobe whose two enclosed white windows have equal widths? Answer NW, NE, SW, or SE.
Does every row and every column of the visible 4-by-4 color grid contain four different dot colors? Answer yes or no.
How many columns are in the checkerboard? Count the vertical stacks of alternating colored squares from left to right.
How many sharp outward points does the single large filled star have? Count only the outer tips, not the inward notches.
Which equal-width half of the filled survey silhouette has the greater mean height above the common baseline: LEFT or RIGHT?
Does the teal distribution contain more visible area to the left or to the right of the dashed divider? Answer left or right.
Circularly slide each horizontal band until its cyan square is leftmost. Ignore the cyan column. Which symbol do the dark squares form?
Trace the navy route. Which matching-color checkpoint pair is farther apart when distance is measured along the route: cyan or orange?
Following the single dark cord from START to END, do the five large colored beads read the same forward and backward? Answer yes or no.
How many separate upward points does the single blue trident have? Count every pointed prong connected to its stem. Answer with a number.
Starting at the green start dot and following the one dark trace, which checkpoint is reached first: orange or violet? Answer orange or violet.
In the one connected dark tree, is the green marker on the unique route joining the red and blue markers? Answer yes or no. Ignore pale corner marks.
How many long horizontal staff lines run continuously from the left barline to the right end? Ignore notes and short ledger marks. Answer 4, 5, or 6.
Follow the single black railway from the orange terminal to the blue terminal. Do you reach the cyan station before the yellow station? Answer yes or no.
A gold ring marks a checkpoint on the teal route. Following the route itself, not a straight line, which endpoint is closer to the checkpoint? Answer LEFT or RIGHT.
Which half of the cyan route has more total vertical travel: left or right? Add every upward and downward change within each side of the dashed divider. Answer left or right.
Trace the navy route from the green START ring to the red FINISH ring. What is the longest uninterrupted run of cyan checkpoints encountered along the route? Answer 1, 2, or 3.
Trace the navy route from the green ring to the red ring. Add 1 at each cyan ring and subtract 1 at each orange ring. Does the running total ever go below zero? Answer yes or no.
The navy thread is one connected trace through R, A, and B. Rotate each candidate field 180 degrees, then choose the candidate whose four-window self-crossing signature matches R.
Which color has the same left-to-right rank in both strips? Answer red, teal, or violet.
Which candidate has the same complete clockwise bead-color order as R after its left-right reflection?
Which labeled lane has the same number of cyan dots on the left as amber dots on the right? Answer A, B, C, or D.
Does the trace in the left plot cross its dashed horizontal baseline before the trace in the right plot? Answer yes or no.
Is the reachable marker pair in the left, center, or right panel? A route may pass through a doorway but not through dark ink.
Which colored sample keeps the same horizontal rank—leftmost, middle, or rightmost—in both panels? Answer coral, blue, or green.
Reading the four colored spots from top to bottom on each butterfly wing, is the color order the same on both wings? Answer yes or no.
Does the black corner rank equal the number of large red hearts in the card center? Ignore the small corner suit mark. Answer yes or no.
The inward tips of the four detached pointers mark the four corners of an invisible rectangle. Is that rectangle wider or taller? Answer wider or taller.
Do the two outlined OPPOSITE FACES show exactly seven dark pips in total? Count only dark circular pips inside the two outlined face squares. Answer yes or no.
Look at the two separated die tiles. Count the dark circular pips inside each tile, ignoring the frame. Do the two counts add to exactly seven? Answer yes or no.
Count white square pockets completely surrounded by each colored rectangle, using edge-sharing connectivity. Do cyan and orange have the same odd/even hole parity?
